title: FRED: A Wafer-scale Fabric for 3D Parallel DNN Training
problem: Current wafer-scale interconnect topologies (e.g., 2D mesh) lack the flexibility to simultaneously support tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism in DNN training, causing collective communications to contend for shared links and inflating training time.
motivation: Wafer-scale systems offer extremely high on-wafer bandwidth but existing static topologies cannot reconfigure to form the non-overlapping communication groups required by hybrid 3D parallelism.
method: FRED distributes tiny routing switches (microswitches) across a silicon wafer to interconnect processing chips (chiplets), allowing data paths to flexibly adjust without any link becoming a bottleneck. Rather than routing all data to a central processor to combine results, these in-network switches start combining data partway through the network, reducing the total traffic. The network maps different parallelism types—data parallelism (processing different datasets), tensor parallelism (splitting model layers), and pipeline parallelism (sequential training stages)—to separate communication groups, so they don't compete for the same links.
key_novelty: Embedding reconfigurable microswitches across the wafer that can combine data in-network lets any arbitrary group of processing chips communicate without interference.
contributions: FRED wafer-scale fabric architecture with microswitches providing nonblocking connectivity for arbitrary collective communication groups.
In-switch collective execution that partially aggregates reduction results at network nodes, cutting traffic.
Evaluation across multiple parallelism strategies showing 1.34-1.87x end-to-end training speedup over 2D Mesh wafer-scale baselines for ResNet-152, Transformer-17B, GPT-3, and Transformer-1T.
Analysis of the topology's suitability for diverse 3D parallelism configurations in large-scale DNN training.

metrics.speedup: 1.34-1.87x end-to-end training time improvement over 2D Mesh wafer-scale baseline (ResNet-152: 1.76x, Transformer-17B: 1.87x, GPT-3: 1.34x, Transformer-1T: 1.4x)

limitations: Cost and manufacturing complexity of integrating microswitches across a full wafer, and the scalability of microswitch routing logic, are not discussed.
primary_theme: reconfigurable wafer-scale network-on-wafer for hybrid parallel DNN training
